changes.before: As introduced, would add RSA 674:81-83, define data centers, and authorize municipalities to permit data centers in commercial or industrial zones with utility capacity confirmation, noise limits near residential districts, and design/siting standards. Senate amendment reportedly broadened the bill and NHMA opposed it because it would require municipalities to permit data centers on land that permits commercial or industrial uses.
changes.after: Introduced SB439 would add RSA 674:81–84, with a 10 percent on-site enterprise-computing exclusion, discretionary municipal permitting in commercial/industrial zones, and utility-capacity, transit-separation, noise and design/siting conditions. The Senate-amended January 29, 2026/0176s text instead proposes RSA 674:81–83, a 25 percent on-site exclusion, data centers allowed in commercial/industrial districts subject to local land-use regulations, and planning-board rulemaking with local legislative-body approval. The compared Senate text omits the introduced prescriptive utility/noise/siting clauses. These are distinct proposed versions, not enacted zoning rights; the later House proposed amendment is not treated as adopted.
